raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose and source

Pair the BF16 `f_b_proj` / `g_b_proj` projections into one cached batched matmul. LoRA-configured models retain the original Linear path, including adapters installed after postload; non-BF16 weights also retain the fallback. Compatible postload weight refreshes update the cache in place to preserve CUDA-graph addresses. First load or incompatible shape/dtype/device allocates new storage and requires graph recapture.

Published head: `47895f99d0b9e52a850285e223f597327691e6a8` on fixed main `32551991b9aff4d8af837d640e3adcd9609f7d75`. The final source has a substantial small-M paired-operation microbenchmark benefit, but the latest standalone standard serving run **does not establish a stable C32 end-to-end gain**.

## Controlled follow-up, 2026-10-26 (local candidate; code not pushed)

A new A0 -> P0 -> P1 -> A1 cycle tests the paired projection with a local compile-compatible view (`narrow -> unflatten -> transpose`, source SHA256 `c4b9ade1bfc00e33ecdd7dafdd43c0fb36cc482258a65babfd8bcf5c28118550`). The published code head above remains unchanged. The view change fixes this PR's padded/nonzero-offset M=1 fullgraph regression: the old source gives 1 failure / 1 pass for the two added tests; the local full suite gives 9 passes. This is not evidence of a baseline upstream serving defect.

All four arms used the same fixed MAIN79 image and [DeepGEMM #448](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/448) correctness extension, #60567 mHC warmup and the local NVIDIA KPool warmup. Each had a separate container and compile-cache copy, with the same initial seed and the relevant mHC/KPool entries removed before startup. All 16 mHC and 8 KPool keys existed at readiness, with **zero new keys during requests**. These common changes are not attributed to paired projection. The startup mnnvl all-reduce probe fell back to the same single-node trtllm backend in all arms; this is a condition of this measurement, not a complete communication optimization certification.

The same stock protocol described below was kept: 1952 formal requests per arm, C1 reference, three 512-request 2K/128 C32 blocks, and three 128-request mixed 2K/32K blocks. All **7808 formal requests**, 48 natural-stop gold questions, and 384 candidate real-weight finite/bitwise output comparisons passed. The 520 workload warmup requests and 32 first/repeat probes are checked separately and excluded from formal aggregates. All formal durations and tails are retained.

| Arm | Primary C32 output tok/s | Primary TTFT p95 (s) | Primary E2EL p95 (s) | C1 output tok/s | Mixed C32 output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A0 baseline | 744.548 | 1.957995 | 5.860297 | 110.180 | 160.739 |
| P0 local candidate | 747.045 | 2.089758 | 5.830634 | 111.399 | 160.890 |
| P1 local candidate | 746.509 | 2.098413 | 5.875038 | 111.393 | 160.906 |
| A1 baseline return | 745.658 | 2.090994 | 5.861095 | 110.206 | 160.786 |

Across the four candidate/baseline comparisons, primary throughput changes range from **+0.114% to +0.335%**, and primary TTFT p95 changes from **-0.059% to +7.171%**. Baseline A1/A0 drift is +0.149%. The prespecified throughput hurdle was >1.000% for each candidate against both baselines, with no >5% TTFT/E2EL p95 regression in any workload. **The gate was not met; a stable comprehensive serving gain is still not established.**

Model compilation mode was NONE, with CUDA graphs enabled; the standalone fullgraph tests are separate evidence and do not certify whole-model piecewise compilation. The shared native extension differs from older experiments, so old/new percentages are not a one-factor estimate of warmup's effect. This is one ordered ABBA cycle, not independent-trial significance, a broad model evaluation, latest-main binary acceptance or production TP16/cache integration. The local compile fix is not published as part of this evidence-only update.

## Earlier published-head standard end-to-end measurement

8x H20, GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 checkpoint, TP8/DP1/EP8, `max_num_seqs=32`, batch-token budget 8192, long-prefill threshold 2048, BF16 KV with 30 GiB/GPU, context 1M. MTP, native APC and external KV transfer were disabled. All arms used the same MAIN79 (`79d5c9379`) runtime plus the existing #62479 producer, model/tokenizer bytes, dependencies and auto backend; #62603 was absent. Only the relevant PR's Python file was overlaid for each candidate. This validates those source overlays, not a rebuilt current-main binary.

Stock `vllm bench serve` was used with fixed seeded custom JSONL inputs produced using its `RandomDataset`, `--save-detailed`, `--request-rate inf`, temperature 0, `--ignore-eos`, fixed 128-token output, `--ready-check-timeout-sec 0` and `--num-warmups 0`. Primary: three 512-request C32 blocks, each 2048 input tokens. Reference: 32 requests at C1. Secondary: three 128-request C32 blocks, a fixed 3:1 mix of 2048/32768-token inputs. Separate validated shape warmups (2 C1, 64 C32 and 64 mixed requests) preceded formal measurement. Each arm also passed the same 12 synthetic gold questions, including 8K/32K inputs, with a separate natural-stop 4096-token cap.

The prespecified primary is **sum of reported output tokens / sum of all three stock durations**, not the median block or a sum across different workloads. All blocks, pauses and tails are retained. Each arm completed all 1952 formal requests with zero failures and matching prompt/generation/request counters, cache-hit zero and MTP disabled. Input generator/tokenizer fingerprints matched across arms. A configured torch profiler was inactive during formal measurement; separate diagnostic traces are excluded.

The fixed actual order was **A0b -> P -> K -> A1**, not randomized or adjacent independent A/B pairs; this table displays only this PR's candidate and the two shared baselines. Initial compiler caches were separate copies from stopped owned runs: A0b from the earlier standard baseline, P from its earlier single-PR run, and K from an earlier baseline run. A1 copied A0b's cache after A0b completed formal measurement and its separate profile. Only seven approved compiler-cache directories were copied, not KV/model state, result files or private venvs. Source hashes and common model settings were verified, but equal initial JIT-variant coverage is not proven.

| Arm | Primary C32 output tok/s (blocks 0 / 1 / 2) | Pooled primary | C1 reference | Mixed C32 blocks 0 / 1 / 2 (pooled) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Baseline before | 750.823 / 730.712 / 752.492 | 744.543 | 110.467 | 162.091 / 162.069 / 162.052 (162.071) |
| P: this PR only | 732.831 / 749.974 / 751.854 | 744.787 | 111.493 | 162.302 / 162.340 / 162.508 (162.383) |
| Baseline return | 751.397 / 752.103 / 751.518 | 751.673 | 110.203 | 161.476 / 162.333 / 162.284 (162.030) |

P versus the before / return baseline: primary **+0.033% / -0.916%**, C1 +0.929% / +1.170%, mixed +0.193% / +0.218%. C1 shows an approximately 1% observation in this MTP-off 2K/128 setting; the primary C32 comparison does not support a consistent net gain.

Pooled primary C32 request latencies, with every block retained:

| Arm | TTFT p95 (s) | TPOT p50 / p95 (ms) | E2EL p99 (s) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline before | 2.075338 | 30.752 / 40.422 | 7.831840 |
| P: this PR only | 2.059919 | 33.661 / 40.199 | 7.790771 |
| Baseline return | 2.063535 | 30.732 / 39.343 | 6.791837 |

P's median TPOT is higher than both baselines; its p95 TPOT and p99 end-to-end latency are also worse than the return baseline. The C1 throughput observation does not override these C32 tradeoffs.

Stock TTFT can include an empty first choices chunk; ITLs are SSE choices-chunk gaps, not individual-token timing. Detailed raw JSON, CLI stdout/stderr, counter acceptances and all block durations are retained. The stock result does not independently expose each request's server token IDs or finish/DONE/usage provenance. Three blocks within one sequential run are not independent experiments or confidence intervals. There is no SLA or statistically established general serving speedup. The return baseline reused a mature owned compilation-cache copy, so the before/return difference is not attributable solely to hardware drift. The approximately 2.4-second pauses in the first baseline and P run remain included; a same-window HC compilation artifact is a diagnostic clue, not established causation.

The executed stock CLI form below uses archived fixture/output paths supplied through variables; these are not new upstream benchmark targets:

```bash
uv run --no-project --offline --no-sync --python .venv/bin/python .venv/bin/python -B -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main bench serve \
  --backend openai --host 127.0.0.1 --port 28401 --endpoint /v1/completions \
  --model "$MODEL" --tokenizer "$MODEL" --served-model-name GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --dataset-name custom --custom-dataset-path "$DATASET" --custom-output-len 128 \
  --skip-chat-template --no-oversample --disable-shuffle --request-rate inf \
  --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 32 --num-warmups 0 --ready-check-timeout-sec 0 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 0 --seed 20261023 --trust-remote-code \
  --save-result --save-detailed --result-dir "$RESULT_DIR" --result-filename "$RESULT_FILE" \
  --disable-tqdm --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el,client_queue_time --metric-percentiles 50,95,99
```

## Correctness and tests

**7 H20 tests passed, 0 skipped**, using real installed modules and constructor paths: four BF16 shapes, non-BF16 fallback, CUDA-graph replay after refit, and a nonzero LoRA adapter installed after postload. The graph test first produced 6 passes/1 failure against an earlier revision of this PR that replaced cache storage, then passed with the in-place storage fix. This fixes a regression introduced during this PR's development, not a newly discovered baseline upstream defect.

The serving candidate additionally passed **192 finite/bitwise comparisons** after real checkpoint loading: first/middle/last of 34 KDA layers, 8 ranks, M=1/32/2048/8192, both outputs. These use real checkpoint weights with deterministic synthetic activations; they are not measurements of actual-request intermediate activations or whole-model bit identity. All arms' 12 synthetic gold answers passed; this is not a general model evaluation suite.

Reviewer command in a configured checkout:

```bash
uv run --no-project --offline --no-sync --python .venv/bin/python .venv/bin/python -B -m pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_paired_projection.py -v
```

The actual isolated UV runners used frozen source/dependency hashes and the complete test file. Changed-file hooks, including Python 3.12 mypy in the pre-commit environment, passed; an additional wrong-environment mypy failure is retained separately. Native, LMCache and producer files remained unchanged.

## Microbenchmark and earlier serving limits

Final-source H20 paired-operation measurement used real BF16 ColumnParallelLinear modules, strict CUPTI graph replay/cold L2, three ABBA blocks and untimed warmup. It measures the full `call_fn` GPU activity span, not CPU dispatch or whole-layer/model latency. Both outputs were bitwise equal before and after timing.

| M | Two Linear GPU span (us) | Paired GPU span (us) | Time reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 5.872 | 2.720 | +53.678% |
| 4 | 5.848 | 2.752 | +52.941% |
| 32 | 5.880 | 2.816 | +52.111% |
| 2048 | 17.424 | 17.720 | -1.699% |
| 8192 | 48.800 | 40.624 | +16.755% |

M2048 regressed in two blocks; M8192 improved in all three. These results do not predict compiled serving performance. Original micro result SHA256: `e1106c548e0497dd430acc29f7a96fe71816bf94fc442b621318901050e8a2f1`.

Historical custom-client MTP-off A0/P/A1 serving is retained separately: the P C32 block rates were **649.138 / 758.354 / 759.621** output tok/s. Pooling every block's output and full wall time gave P 718.460 versus baselines 754.070/757.330, **-4.72%/-5.13%**. Its predeclared block-median results were much closer (+0.61%/+0.06%), while p95 first-output and median TPOT worsened. These older custom-client definitions differ from the new stock benchmark; they are not replaced, pooled with it or used to discard its slow block. Neither episode establishes stable comprehensive serving acceleration.

## Related work and disclosure

Narrow open-PR/body searches refreshed on 2026-10-23 found no direct replacement for paired `f_b_proj`/`g_b_proj`: #62956's SM121 skinny-GEMM scope excludes these projections; #56327 concerns LoRA mappings and #57638/#57678 loader/cache lifecycle work. #61662 is an opt-in ROCm MI355X decode layer. Search results are not proof of exhaustive absence of overlap. This updates the existing PR.

AI assistance was used for implementation, experiment preparation and analysis; the human author remains accountable for reviewing every changed line and the tests. The recorded published-head pre-run admission, DCO, pre-commit and documentation checks passed, while review remained required. No CI admission label or rerun was requested; these checks do not establish complete GPU CI or maintainer approval.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Preserve real KDA projection outputs under pairing, refit, and LoRA.
+
+The input is merged q|k|v|b|f_a|g_a and the output is two gate projections.
+Guard against bypassing adapters or replaying stale weights after a refit.
+Real single-rank layers and the existing LoRA wrapper are the cheapest path;
+attention state and a full model are unnecessary for these projection contracts.
+"""
+
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+from transformers import Glm5NextConfig, Glm5NextTextConfig
+
+from vllm.config import LoRAConfig, ModelConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+from vllm.forward_context import set_forward_context
+from vllm.lora.layers import ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA, LoRAMapping
+from vllm.lora.punica_wrapper import get_punica_wrapper
+from vllm.models.glm5next.common.kda import Glm5NextLinearAttention
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_default_torch_dtype
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="CUDA-only BF16 GEMM"
+)
+
+HEAD_DIM = 128
+LOCAL_NUM_HEADS = 8
+LOCAL_PROJ_SIZE = HEAD_DIM * LOCAL_NUM_HEADS
+F_A_OFFSET = 3 * LOCAL_PROJ_SIZE + LOCAL_NUM_HEADS
+ROW_WIDTH = F_A_OFFSET + 2 * HEAD_DIM
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def layer_factory(tmp_path, dist_init):
+    @contextmanager
+    def create(dtype, *, enable_lora=False):
+        config = Glm5NextTextConfig(
+            architectures=["Glm5NextForCausalLM"],
+            hidden_size=128,
+            intermediate_size=256,
+            num_hidden_layers=1,
+            num_attention_heads=8,
+            num_key_value_heads=8,
+            vocab_size=256,
+            max_position_embeddings=256,
+            first_k_dense_replace=1,
+            n_routed_experts=4,
+            num_experts_per_tok=1,
+            layer_types=["linear_attention"],
+            linear_num_heads=LOCAL_NUM_HEADS,
+            linear_head_dim=HEAD_DIM,
+            linear_conv_kernel_dim=4,
+            linear_lower_bound=-5.0,
+            linear_attn_config={
+                "num_heads": LOCAL_NUM_HEADS,
+                "head_dim": HEAD_DIM,
+                "short_conv_kernel_size": 4,
+                "gate_lower_bound": -5.0,
+            },
+        )
+        Glm5NextConfig(
+            architectures=["Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration"],
+            text_config=config.to_dict(),
+        ).save_pretrained(tmp_path)
+        lora_config = (
+            LoRAConfig(max_lora_rank=8, max_loras=1, lora_dtype=dtype)
+            if enable_lora
+            else None
+        )
+        vllm_config = VllmConfig(
+            model_config=ModelConfig(
+                model=str(tmp_path),
+                dtype="bfloat16" if dtype == torch.bfloat16 else "float32",
+                max_model_len=256,
+                skip_tokenizer_init=True,
+                enforce_eager=True,
+            ),
+            lora_config=lora_config,
+            additional_config={"kda_prefill_backend": "triton"},
+        )
+        with (
+            set_current_vllm_config(vllm_config),
+            torch.device("cuda"),
+            set_default_torch_dtype(dtype),
+        ):
+            layer = Glm5NextLinearAttention(
+                config, vllm_config, prefix="model.layers.0.linear_attn"
+            )
+            for parameter in layer.parameters():
+                torch.nn.init.uniform_(parameter, -0.1, 0.1)
+            yield layer, vllm_config
+
+    return create
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_tokens", [1, 5, 64, 256])
+def test_paired_fg_projection_bit_identical(layer_factory, num_tokens: int):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    with layer_factory(torch.bfloat16) as (layer, _):
+        layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.bfloat16)
+        projected = torch.randn(num_tokens, ROW_WIDTH, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        f_a = projected[:, F_A_OFFSET : F_A_OFFSET + HEAD_DIM]
+        g_a = projected[:, F_A_OFFSET + HEAD_DIM : F_A_OFFSET + 2 * HEAD_DIM]
+        g1, g2 = layer._paired_fg_projections(projected)
+        assert torch.equal(g1, layer.f_b_proj(f_a)[0])
+        assert torch.equal(g2, layer.g_b_proj(g_a)[0])
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_paired_fg_graph_replay_uses_refitted_weights(layer_factory):
+    with layer_factory(torch.bfloat16) as (layer, _):
+        layer.f_b_proj.weight.fill_(1 / HEAD_DIM)
+        layer.g_b_proj.weight.fill_(2 / HEAD_DIM)
+        layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.bfloat16)
+        projected = torch.ones(5, ROW_WIDTH, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        f_a = projected[:, F_A_OFFSET : F_A_OFFSET + HEAD_DIM]
+        g_a = projected[:, F_A_OFFSET + HEAD_DIM : F_A_OFFSET + 2 * HEAD_DIM]
+        stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+        stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+        with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+            for _ in range(3):
+                layer._paired_fg_projections(projected)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            actual_f, actual_g = layer._paired_fg_projections(projected)
+        # Keep the captured storage alive so allocator reuse cannot hide stale data.
+        captured_weight = layer._paired_fg_weight
+        layer.f_b_proj.weight.fill_(0.5 / HEAD_DIM)
+        layer.g_b_proj.weight.fill_(1 / HEAD_DIM)
+        layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.bfloat16)
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        assert captured_weight is not None
+        assert torch.equal(actual_f, layer.f_b_proj(f_a)[0])
+        assert torch.equal(actual_g, layer.g_b_proj(g_a)[0])
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_paired_fg_weight_disabled_for_non_bf16(layer_factory):
+    with layer_factory(torch.float32) as (layer, _):
+        layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.float32)
+        assert layer._paired_fg_weight is None
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_lora_gate_projections_are_used_after_postload(layer_factory):
+    with layer_factory(torch.bfloat16, enable_lora=True) as (layer, config):
+        layer.in_proj_qkvbfg_a.weight.fill_(1 / 128)
+        layer.f_b_proj.weight.zero_()
+        layer.g_b_proj.weight.zero_()
+        # The manager installs wrappers after the ordinary weight processing.
+        layer.process_weights_after_loading(torch.bfloat16)
+        punica = get_punica_wrapper(16, 1, "cuda", lora_config=config.lora_config)
+        observed: dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]] = {"f_b_proj": [], "g_b_proj": []}
+        handles = []
+        for name, value in (("f_b_proj", 1), ("g_b_proj", 2)):
+            wrapper = ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA(layer.get_submodule(name))
+            wrapper.create_lora_weights(1, config.lora_config)
+            wrapper.set_mapping(punica)
+            lora_a = torch.zeros(8, HEAD_DIM, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            lora_b = torch.zeros(LOCAL_PROJ_SIZE, 8, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            lora_a[0].fill_(1 / HEAD_DIM)
+            lora_b[:, 0].fill_(value)
+            wrapper.set_lora(0, lora_a, lora_b)
+            layer.set_submodule(name, wrapper)
+
+            def capture(module, inputs, output, name=name):
+                observed[name].append(output[0].clone())
+
+            handles.append(wrapper.register_forward_hook(capture))
+        punica.update_metadata(
+            LoRAMapping([1, 1, 1], [1], is_prefill=True), [1], 1, 256
+        )
+        try:
+            # The real profiling path needs no recurrent state; gates run first.
+            with set_forward_context(None, config, num_tokens=3):
+                layer(torch.ones(3, 128, dtype=torch.bfloat16), torch.arange(3))
+        finally:
+            for handle in handles:
+                handle.remove()
+        for name, value in (("f_b_proj", 1), ("g_b_proj", 2)):
+            assert len(observed[name]) == 1
+            assert torch.equal(
+                observed[name][0],
+                torch.full((3, LOCAL_PROJ_SIZE), value, dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            )

@@ -297,6 +297,11 @@ def __init__(
         # Lazily-built merged q|k|v conv weight (built on first forward, after
         # weights are loaded). See _forward.
         self._merged_conv_weight: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        # Paired projection storage is refreshed after loading and reused on
+        # compatible refits to preserve CUDA graph references.
+        self._paired_fg_weight: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        # LoRA wrappers are installed after weight processing.
+        self._use_paired_fg = vllm_config.lora_config is None
 
         self.A_log = nn.Parameter(
             torch.empty(1, 1, self.local_num_heads, 1, dtype=torch.float32)
@@ -382,6 +387,48 @@ def _a_log_weight_loader(param, loaded_weight):
                 state_len=self.conv_size - 1
             )
 
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self, act_dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+        # KDA projections stay BF16 (fp8 checkpoints omit their scales).
+        # Other dtypes and LoRA keep the two-Linear path.
+        if not self._use_paired_fg or self.f_b_proj.weight.dtype != torch.bfloat16:
+            self._paired_fg_weight = None
+            return
+
+        paired_weight = (
+            torch.stack([self.f_b_proj.weight, self.g_b_proj.weight])
+            .transpose(1, 2)
+            .contiguous()
+        )
+        cached = self._paired_fg_weight
+        if (
+            cached is not None
+            and cached.shape == paired_weight.shape
+            and cached.dtype == paired_weight.dtype
+            and cached.device == paired_weight.device
+        ):
+            cached.copy_(paired_weight)
+        else:
+            self._paired_fg_weight = paired_weight
+
+    def _paired_fg_projections(
+        self, projected: torch.Tensor
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        """Run the paired f_b/g_b projections on the merged projection output.
+
+        f_a and g_a are adjacent head_dim-wide shards of each ``projected``
+        row (after q|k|v|b), read in place as one strided batch — no copies.
+        """
+        assert self._paired_fg_weight is not None
+        fg = projected.as_strided(
+            (2, projected.size(0), self.head_dim),
+            (self.head_dim, projected.stride(0), 1),
+            projected.storage_offset()
+            + 3 * self.local_projection_size
+            + self.local_num_heads,
+        )
+        g1, g2 = torch.bmm(fg, self._paired_fg_weight).unbind(0)
+        return g1, g2
+

         self,
         q: torch.Tensor,

+            # One batched GEMM for both gate projections (paired post-load).
+            g1, g_proj_states = self._paired_fg_projections(projected)
+        else:
+            g1 = self.f_b_proj(f_a)[0]
+            g_proj_states = self.g_b_proj(g_a)[0]

-
-        g_proj_states = self.g_b_proj(g_a)[0]

         g2 = g_proj_states.reshape(-1, self.local_num_heads, self.head_dim)

These profiles were collected on my commit [0b874994c3](https://github.com/qianlihuang/vllm/commit/0b874994c3fb6edd6e8deb9651be2ed96e177059).
Setup: 8× NVIDIA H200, GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 checkpoint with BF16 KDA projections, TP1/DP8/EP, DecodeBenchConnector, ISL131072/OSL512, concurrency128, MTP3 with synthetic unconditional acceptance rates [0.8, 0.6, 0.5].

[baseline-dp0.pt.trace.json.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33416305/baseline-dp0.pt.trace.json.gz)
[bmm-dp0.pt.trace.json.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33416306/bmm-dp0.pt.trace.json.gz)

The DP0 profile shows 34 fewer BF16-linear kernel launches per step (431 → 397, one fewer per KDA layer). Summed BF16-linear kernel time decreased from 5.457 to 5.363 ms/step, saving approximately 94 µs (~1.7% of this category).
